claims.text: The magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys under low applied fields are governed by the degree of chemical short-range order established during deposition.
Higher chemical short-range order produces a more gradual magnetostructural transformation.
Higher chemical short-range order lowers and homogenizes the nucleation barrier for domain switching.
Lower chemical short-range order promotes a sharp, strongly hysteretic first-order transition.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films have a single-phase ordered, likely hexagonal structure.
The film geometry provides a high surface-to-volume ratio.
A controlled low-temperature anneal can modify chemical short-range order without significant phase separation or grain coarsening.
Fe-, Mn-, and Ni-centered chemical short-range order is associated with the distribution of strain fields in the nanocrystalline matrix.
Enhanced short-range order produces more uniform magnetic and lattice environments.
More uniform magnetic and lattice environments facilitate a smoother magnetostructural transformation.
A smoother transformation spreads the entropy change over a wider temperature interval.
Spreading the transformation over a wider temperature interval reduces hysteretic losses.
A lower or more random short-range-order state yields a sharper transition with higher latent heat and larger hysteresis.
The proposed annealing treatment will increase chemical short-range order.
Annealed samples with increased short-range order will exhibit a broader and less hysteretic magnetocaloric response than the as-deposited baseline.
The as-deposited baseline exhibits a sharp, high-magnitude, narrow, and hysteretic entropy-change peak under low-field cycling.
The predictions apply near the magnetostructural transition under low applied fields when grain growth and phase separation remain minimal.
The proposed effect may cease to hold when annealing changes the nanostructure or induces additional phase transformations.
